On this page

Connecting Telegram ​

Telegram is a channel — a second surface onto the same PRIME, the same runs, and the same memory. Nothing about the orchestrator changes; the channel adapter translates between Telegram's API and Saidi's chat session model.

Set it up ​

  1. Create a bot with @BotFather and copy the token.
  2. Open Settings → Telegram in the Saidi UI.
  3. Paste the token and save. The adapter connects and starts receiving updates.

Link your identity ​

A Telegram account is not automatically you. The adapter keeps a channel identity record mapping a Telegram user id to a Saidi member, and an unlinked sender gets nothing.

Link from the Telegram settings page, or by sending the pairing command the bot replies with on first contact. Once linked:

  • Your messages resolve to your member record.
  • Runs you start from Telegram carry your createdBy, so your budget, permissions, and connections govern them.
  • Your personal memory (memory/members/<userId>/global.md) is the one that gets injected.

An unlinked chat is not a logged-out chat — it is a stranger

Do not add the bot to a group and assume the group is authenticated. Identity is per-sender, and each sender must be linked.

Sessions ​

Each linked chat maps to a durable chat session. The conversation persists across restarts, and the same session is what the web UI shows — start a thought in Telegram and finish it in the browser.

What works from Telegram ​

  • Chat with PRIME — the full toolbelt is available, so you can start runs, ask projects questions, and record memory from your phone.
  • Run notices — lifecycle transitions arrive as messages: finished, failed, waiting on you. These come off the same run-notice bus that feeds the reflex engine.
  • Runs UI — an inline keyboard for listing runs, opening one, and replying into it.
  • Approvals — a pending approval renders with Approve/Deny buttons for that exact change.

Formatting ​

Telegram's markdown dialect is narrow and unforgiving — an unbalanced backtick breaks a whole message. The adapter normalises Saidi's output before sending: fences, inline code, links, and long messages are converted and split at safe boundaries. If a code block looks mangled in Telegram but fine in the browser, that is where to look.

Practical notes ​

  • Keep the token in .env, not in a repo. It is a full bot credential.
  • Long output belongs in the web UI. Telegram is excellent for approving, steering, and being told something finished; it is a poor place to read a diff.
  • Files sent via send_file arrive as Telegram documents or photos.
